Short title and extent

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February, 1910]
An Act to provide for the prevention of the spread of
Dourine
WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the
prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as follows:‑
1‑‑(1)
This Act may be called the Dourine Act, 1910.

Definition

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]
An Act to provide for the prevention of the spread of Dourine
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
2.‑(1)Definition-- In this Act, the expressions
"inspector" and "veterinary practitioner" mean,
respectively, the officers appointed as such under this Act, acting within the
local limits for which they are so appointed.
(2) The provisions of this Act in
so far as they relate to entire horses shall, if the Subs.
by A. O., 1937, for "L. G.".[Provincial Government], by
notification as aforesaid, so directs, apply also to entire asses used for mule
breeding purposes.

Registration of horses

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]

WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
3. Registration of horses The Subs. by A.
O., 1937, for "L. G.". [Provincial Government] may, by
notification as aforesaid, make such orders as it thinks fit directing and
regulating the registration of entire horses maintained for breeding purposes.

Appointment of inspectors and veterinary practitioners

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]
An Act to provide for the prevention of the spread of Dourine
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
4. Appointment of inspectors and veterinary practitioners (1) The Subs. by A. O., 1937, for "L. G.".
[Provincial Government] may, by notification as aforesaid, appoint any persons
it thinks fit to be inspectors, and any qualified veterinary surgeons to be
veterinary practitioners, veterinary under this Act, and to exercise and
perform, within any area practitioners. prescribed by the notification, the
powers conferred and duties imposed by this Act upon such officers
respectively.
(2) Every person so appointed
shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of the Pakistan Penal
Code. XLV of 1860

Powers of inspector

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]

WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
5. Powers of inspector An inspector may, subject to such rules as
the 1[Provincial Government] may make in this behalf,‑
(a) enter and search any
building, field or other place for the purpose of ascertaining whether there is
therein any horse which is affected with dourine; The
word "and" omitted by the Dourine (Amdt.) Act, 1920 (8 of 1920),
section 2.*
(b) prohibit, by order in
writing, the owner or keeper of any horse, which in his opinion is affected
with dourine, from using such horse for breeding purposes, pending examination
by the veterinary practitioner;
Clause
(c) ins., ibid. [(c) direct, by order in writing, the owner or keeper of
any horse which, in the opinion of the inspectors, is affected with dourine to
remove it or permit it to be removed for the purpose of segregation to a place
specified in the order, and such direction shall be sufficient authority for
the detention of the horse in that place for that purpose.]

Duties of inspector

WHEREAS it is expedient to

6. Duties of inspector An inspector issuing an order under section
5, The word, brackets and letter "clause (b)"
omitted by the Dourine (Amdt.) Act, 1920 (8 of 1920), s. 3.* * shall
forthwith forward a copy of such order to the veterinary practitioner.

Inspection of horses

[25th February,
1910]

WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
7. Inspection of horses. A veterinary practitioner receiving a copy
of an order forwarded under section 6 shall, as soon as possible after receipt
of such copy, examine the horse mentioned therein, and may for such purpose
enter any building, field or other place.

Powers of veterinary practitioner

ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]

WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
8. Powers of veterinary practitioner, A veterinary practitioner may ---
(a) cancel any order issued under
section 5 The word, brackets and letter "clause
(b)" omitted ibid., s. 4.* *; or
(b) if on microscopical
examination Ins. ibid., s. 4. [or by other
scientific test] he finds that any horse is affected with dourine,‑
(i) in the case of an entire
horse, cause it to be castrated,
Subs.
ibid., for the original sub‑clause (ii).(ii) in the case of a
mare, with the previous sanction of such authority as the Subs. by A. O., 1937, for "L,. G.",[Provincial
Government] may appoint in this behalf, or, if so empowered by the Subs. by A. O., 1937, for "L,. G.",[Provincial
Government], without such sanction, cause it to be destroyed.

Compensation for horse destroyed, etc

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]
An Act to provide for the prevention of the spread of Dourine
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
9. Compensation for horse destroyed, etc. When any horse is
castrated or destroyed under section 8, the market‑value of such horse
immediately before it became affected with dourine shall be ascertained; and
the Subs. by A. O., 1937, for "L,. G.",[Provincial
Government] shall pay as compensation to the owner thereof
(a) in the case of a mare which
has been destroyed, or of an entire horse which has died in consequence of
castra tion, such market‑value, and,
(b) in the case of an entire
horse which survives castration, half the amount by which such value has been
dimi nished owing to infection with dourine and castration.

Settlement of compensation

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]
An Act to provide for the prevention of the spread of Dourine
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
10.‑(1) Settlement of compensation A veterinary practitioner
may award, as compensa tion to be paid under section 9 in respect of each horse
castrated or destroyed under section 8, a sum not exceeding two hundred and
fifty rupees.
(2) If, in the opinion of the
veterinary practitioner, the amount which should be paid as such compensation
exceeds two hundred and fifty rupees,
he shall report accordingly to the Collector, who shall decide the amount to be
so paid.

Committees hearing appeals

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]
An Act to provide for the prevention of the spread of Dourine
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
11.‑(1)Committees hearing appeals The Subs. by A. O., 1937, for "L. G.".[Provincial Government]
shall, by rules published in the Subs. ibid., for
"local official Gazette". [official Gazette], make provision
for the constitution of a committee or committees for the hearing of appeals
from decisions under section 10.
(2) Such rules shall provide that
not less than one member of any committee constituted thereunder shall be a
person not in the The original words "employ of
Government" were first subs. by A. O., 1937, and then amended by A. O.,
1961, Art. 2 (with effect from the 23rd March 1956), to read as above.[service
of the Government] or of a local authority.

Appeal

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]
An Act to provide for the prevention of the spread of Dourine
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
12. Any owner may, within two
months from the date of a Appeals decision under section 10, appeal against
such decision to the committee constituted in that behalf by rules made under
section 11, and the decision of such committee shall be final.

Vexations entries and searches

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]
An Act to provide for the prevention of the spread of Dourine
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
13.‑(1) Vexations entries and searches- Whoever, being an
inspector appointed under this Vexatious entries Act, vexatiously and
unnecessarily enters or searches any field, and searches building or other
place, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six
months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
(2) No prosecution under this
section shall be instituted after the expiry of three months from the date on
which the offence has been committed.

15. Penalties. Whoever uses or permits to be used for breeding
purposes ---
(a) any horse which has not been
registered in accordance with the requirements of a notification under section
3. or
Subs. by
the Dourine (Arndt.) Act, 1920 (8 of 1920), s. 6, for the original clauses (b)

sections.description:
Protection to persons acting under Act

THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
THE DOURINE ACT, 1910
ACT No. V of 1910
[25th February,
1910]
An Act to provide for the prevention of the spread of Dourine
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine; It is hereby enacted as
follows:‑
16. Protection to persons acting under Act. No suit, prosecution or
other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything which is, in
good faith, done or intended to be done under this Act.
